target_customer: HR teams at tech companies hiring international employees
problem: Work visa applications such as H-1B were slow and costly; existing tools were built for lawyers rather than HR staff.
business_model: SaaS tracking (free for existing visa tracking) plus fees of 5,000 to 10,000 dollars per application with lawyer review

founders.name: James Richards
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch says he studied in several countries, is qualified to practice law in New York and was on an E-3 visa. Later CEO of Evergrow per YC page.

founders.name: Michael Smith
founders.background_notes: YC page describes him as a programmer, system administrator and IT consultant.

founders.name: Michael Hendrickx
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in TechCrunch only.

founders.name: Ikhsan Maulana
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in TechCrunch only.

competitors.name: LawLogix
competitors.what: Immigration case software built for lawyers

competitors.name: INSzoom
competitors.what: Immigration case software built for lawyers

technical_complexity.rationale: Workflow software for visa filings; the hard part was legal and process knowledge more than engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Legal review network and compliance workflows add stickiness, but incumbents' products already existed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: TriNet bought Teleborder's assets in April 2016 and the team joined TriNet.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (2013-08) says existing tools were priced for lawyers, and claimed Teleborder cut application time by up to 80 percent.

branding.domain_note: teleborder.com did not resolve in this session's network; current ownership unknown.

brand_strength.rationale: Coverage was product and deal focused; no brand-specific press found.

outcome_analysis: Teleborder sold immigration software and lawyer-reviewed filings to HR teams, raised about 1 million dollars in seed funding from Khosla Ventures and others, and grew beyond two founders. TriNet bought its assets in April 2016 and took in the whole team, with no price disclosed. CB Insights marks it Dead because it no longer operates independently, so this reads as a modest exit into a larger HR platform.
notes: Rounds rest on CB Insights (single database): 2013-06-26 seed, amount not stated (total 1.02M across 2 rounds suggests about 20K, not stated); 2014-07-14 seed 1M. Xconomy has a seed financing item dated 2013-09-23 listing a different investor (WeFunder), unverified; dates conflict so the 1M seed may be 2013. TriNet release lists investors including IDG Capital, SV Frontier and 500 Startups, not tied to rounds. Status Inactive in the YC directory is consistent with the asset purchase. Only the YC page and TriNet release were opened for exit facts.
